first: किं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम ।
en: Arjuna said: Best of beings, what is Brahman? What is the self? What is action? What is said to be the basis of beings, and what is called the basis of the gods?
Madhusudana, who is the lord of sacrifice here in this body, and how? And how are you to be known at the time of death by those who are self-controlled?
Krishna said: Brahman is the imperishable, the Supreme. Its own nature is called the self. The creative force that brings beings into existence is called action.
The basis of beings is what perishes. The basis of the gods is the Spirit. And I alone, here in this body, am the lord of sacrifice, best of embodied beings.
One who leaves the body at the time of death remembering me alone comes to my state. There is no doubt about this.

first: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् ।
en: Son of Kunti, whatever state of being a person remembers when leaving the body at the end, to that state he goes, having always been absorbed in it.
So remember me at all times, and fight. With your mind and intellect offered to me, you will surely come to me.
Son of Pritha, one who thinks of the supreme divine Spirit with a mind made steady by practice and not wandering elsewhere goes to that Spirit.
One should remember the all-knowing, the ancient, the ruler, smaller than the smallest, the support of all, whose form is beyond thought, bright as the sun, beyond darkness;
at the time of death, with a steady mind, joined in devotion and by the power of yoga, placing the life-breath fully between the eyebrows, such a person reaches that supreme divine Spirit.
I will tell you briefly about that state which those who know the Veda call the Imperishable, which those free from passion enter, and for which people practise self-restraint.

first: सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च ।
en: Closing all the gates of the body, holding the mind in the heart, placing the life-breath in the head, and staying firm in yoga;
saying Om, the one syllable that is Brahman, and remembering me, one who goes forth leaving the body reaches the highest goal.

first: अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः ।
en: Son of Pritha, I am easy to reach for the yogi who is always steady, who remembers me constantly and every day, with a mind that turns to nothing else.
Having come to me, great souls who have reached the highest perfection are not born again into this passing home of sorrow.
Arjuna, all worlds up to the world of Brahma return again. But on reaching me, son of Kunti, there is no rebirth.
Those who know that a day of Brahma lasts a thousand ages and a night lasts a thousand ages are people who know day and night.
When that day comes, all visible things come forth from the unseen. When the night comes, they dissolve into that same unseen.

first: भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते ।
en: This same crowd of beings, coming into being again and again, dissolves helplessly when night comes, son of Pritha, and comes forth again when day comes.
But beyond that unseen there is another unseen, eternal state, which does not perish when all beings perish.
That unseen is called the Imperishable, and it is said to be the highest goal. Those who reach it do not return. That is my supreme home.

first: पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया ।
en: Son of Pritha, that supreme Spirit, in whom all beings live and by whom all this is filled, can be reached by devotion that turns to nothing else.
Best of the Bharatas, I will now tell you the times at which yogis who leave this world do not return, and the times at which they return.
Fire, light, day, the bright half of the month, the six months when the sun moves north: those who know Brahman and depart then go to Brahman.
Smoke, night, the dark half of the month, the six months when the sun moves south: the yogi who departs then reaches the light of the moon and returns.

first: शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते ।
en: These two paths of the world, the bright and the dark, are thought to be eternal. By one a person does not return; by the other a person returns.

first: नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन ।
en: Son of Pritha, no yogi who knows these two paths is confused. So, Arjuna, be steady in yoga at all times.
Whatever reward is promised for study of the Vedas, sacrifices, austerities and gifts, the yogi who knows this goes beyond it all and reaches the supreme, first state.
